evidenceRecords.population: 1,874 participants without diabetes with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer
evidenceRecords.comparison: Oral metformin 850 mg twice daily plus standard care versus standard care
evidenceRecords.formulation: Release formulation not established in the bounded material inspected
evidenceRecords.finding: Metformin did not demonstrate an overall-survival improvement.
evidenceRecords.limits: Allocation implementation, adherence, censoring and full protocol not independently appraised.

evidenceRecords.population: 167 eligible participants without diabetes with unresectable stage III NSCLC, Zubrod performance status 0–1
evidenceRecords.comparison: Oral metformin escalated to 2,000 mg/day during concurrent chemoradiotherapy and consolidation chemotherapy versus the same cancer treatment alone
evidenceRecords.endpoint: Progression-free survival: time from randomization to RECIST 1.1 progression or death
evidenceRecords.timepoint: One-year survival estimate; HR across follow-up, median 27.7 months among survivors
evidenceRecords.formulation: Release formulation not established in the bounded material inspected
evidenceRecords.finding: Metformin did not demonstrate a progression-free-survival improvement.
evidenceRecords.limits: Supplement 1 protocol and Supplement 2 detailed adherence/covariate analyses unavailable to this assessment. Do not label the HR as a one-year risk ratio or use this grade for overall survival.

evidenceRecords.population: 54 participants without diabetes with unresected locally advanced stage III NSCLC
evidenceRecords.comparison: Chemoradiotherapy plus oral metformin 2,000 mg/day, continued up to 12 months, versus chemoradiotherapy alone
evidenceRecords.timepoint: One-year survival estimate; time-to-event HR over trial follow-up
evidenceRecords.formulation: Release formulation not established in the bounded material inspected
evidenceRecords.finding: This small trial reported worse overall survival with metformin.
evidenceRecords.limits: Protocol and supplements not independently inspected; full review unfinished.

evidenceRecords.population: 151 randomized patients without diabetes after colorectal polyp removal; 133 underwent follow-up colonoscopy
evidenceRecords.comparison: Oral metformin 250 mg daily versus identical placebo
evidenceRecords.endpoint: Prevalence of recurrent colorectal adenoma at follow-up colonoscopy
evidenceRecords.formulation: Release formulation not established in the bounded material inspected
evidenceRecords.finding: Metformin reduced reported one-year adenoma recurrence.
evidenceRecords.limits: Missing-colonoscopy handling, full protocol and numerical discrepancy require full-text reconciliation.

evidenceRecords.population: Nonhospitalized adults aged 30–85 with overweight or obesity, infection confirmed within 3 days and symptoms beginning within 7 days; 1,323 in the modified intention-to-treat population
evidenceRecords.comparison: Immediate-release oral metformin titrated over 6 days to 1,500 mg/day for 14 days versus concurrently randomized control, adjusting for vaccination and the other randomized trial drugs
evidenceRecords.endpoint: Primary composite of hypoxemia (home oxygen saturation ≤93%), emergency-department visit, hospitalization or death
evidenceRecords.finding: Metformin did not demonstrate a reduction in the primary acute COVID-19 composite outcome.
evidenceRecords.limits: Supplementary full intention-to-treat sensitivity analyses and protocol not inspected in this bounded assessment. Use the adjusted estimate; the article warns against naive comparison of absolute event rates across treatment groups enrolled at different times.

evidenceRecords.population: Healthy, predominantly high-functioning older adults, eligibility age 65 years or older; 109 randomized and 94 completers analyzed
evidenceRecords.comparison: Oral metformin titrated to 1,700 mg/day versus placebo, both with supervised progressive resistance training
evidenceRecords.endpoint: Percentage change in total lean body mass measured by DXA
evidenceRecords.timepoint: Baseline to study week 16: 14 weeks of supervised progressive resistance training after a 2-week drug wash-in
evidenceRecords.formulation: Release formulation not established in the bounded material inspected
evidenceRecords.finding: Total lean-body-mass gains during resistance training were smaller with metformin.
evidenceRecords.magnitude: Mean change 0.41% (SD 2.25) with metformin versus 1.95% (SD 2.69) with placebo; between-group P=.003.
evidenceRecords.limits: Updated Appendix S2 and remaining supplement/protocol detail uninspected. The corrected relative-strength result remains nonsignificant (P=.30), but it is excluded from this lean-mass grade. Full-paper correction reconciliation remains unfinished; no currently identified correction changes this narrowly assessed DXA endpoint.
